walk.title: Get started with Mycelium
walk.desc: Capture your AI coding sessions, organize them, and carry what they learned into the next one.
walk.connect.title: Connect the Mycelium CLI
walk.connect.desc:
Mycelium keeps what your AI coding sessions learned and carries it into the next one, in four stages: **Capture → Organize → Learn → Reuse**.
This extension is the editor side of the `mycelium` command you installed with npm — if the sidebar shows your sessions, you're connected.
The Mycelium icon in the left activity bar opens the sidebar; **Actions** at the top lists everything you can do.
[Open settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22mycelium.path%22%5D)
walk.scan.title: Capture: scan your sessions
walk.scan.desc:
Pulls sessions from Claude Code, Codex, Kiro and OpenCode into your Mycelium store. New ones land under **New** in the Folders view.
Scan again any time with the sync icon or the status bar.
Afterwards, every action lives under **Actions** at the top of the Mycelium sidebar (the icon in the left activity bar).
[Scan now](command:mycelium.scan)
walk.summarize.title: Learn: give sessions a summary
walk.summarize.desc:
Gives each session a title, tags, a summary, decisions and to-dos, using your own `claude` or `codex` login. Organizing works much better once sessions have summaries.
Runs up to 25 at a time — run it again for more. You can cancel any time.
[Summarize sessions](command:mycelium.autotagAll)
walk.organize.title: Organize: file sessions into folders
walk.organize.desc:
**Smart organize** suggests a folder for each unfiled session and lets you untick any you disagree with. Or just drag sessions onto folders — a session you place by hand is never moved automatically.
[Smart organize](command:mycelium.organize)
walk.knowledge.title: Learn: extract what a folder knows
walk.knowledge.desc:
Right-click a folder → **Extract Folder Knowledge**. Mycelium writes what its sessions decided and learned into a KNOWLEDGE.md, and shows you the diff before saving anything.
[Extract knowledge](command:mycelium.extractKnowledge)
walk.search.title: Find: search and open an old session
walk.search.desc:
Search by anything you remember — a file, an error, a decision. Open a result to read its summary, decisions and to-dos in one place.
[Search sessions](command:mycelium.search)
walk.resume.title: Reuse: resume or hand off
walk.resume.desc:
**Resume** continues a session in a terminal tab — or in the Claude Code panel, if you have that extension. **Hand off** gives another agent the context — to switch from Claude to Codex mid-task. Merged or split sessions can only be handed off.
Hover a session and press ▶ or ⇄, or use the buttons on its page.
walk.newAgent.title: Reuse: start a new session, already informed
walk.newAgent.desc:
Start an agent in a folder. Mycelium first offers to put that folder's knowledge into the project's AGENTS.md, so the new session starts with what the old ones learned.
[Start an agent](command:mycelium.newAgent)
config.openIn: Where Resume, Hand off and Start New Agent open their terminal.
config.openIn.project: In a window on the session's own project directory (opens one if needed).
config.openIn.this: In this window, whatever folder it has open.
welcome.outdated:
The Mycelium command-line tool is too old for this extension (it needs 0.5.0 or newer).

Update it, then reload the window:
`npm install -g @kevinprk/mycelium`
or `brew upgrade mycelium`
[Reload Window](command:workbench.action.reloadWindow)
capability.untrusted: Mycelium starts agent CLIs and runs commands in your project, so it only runs in folders you trust.
welcome.node:
Mycelium found its command-line tool, but not Node.js, which it needs (version 22.16 or newer).

VS Code may have started without your shell's PATH: start it from a terminal with `code`, or install Node.js from nodejs.org.
[Show log](command:mycelium.showLog)
[Copy diagnostics](command:mycelium.copyDiagnostics)
[Reload Window](command:workbench.action.reloadWindow)
config.claudeOpenIn: Where Resume, Hand off and Start New Agent open a Claude Code session when the Claude Code extension is installed.
config.claudeOpenIn.auto: In the Claude Code panel, unless the Claude Code extension is set to use the terminal (`claudeCode.useTerminal`).
config.claudeOpenIn.panel: Always in the Claude Code panel.
